items.title: Precisely Defining "Elimination" — And Closing the Threefold Scriptural Proof

items.zh: 謂於一切地等想事，諸地等名施設假立，名地等想。即此諸想，於彼所有色等想事，或起增益、或起損減。
items.en: With respect to every event conceived of as earth and so on, the designations "earth" and the rest are established through imputation — this is called the percept of earth and so on. These very percepts, with respect to the events conceived through perception that they concern, either generate superimposition or generate denial.

items.zh: 若於彼事起能增益有體自性執，名增益想；起能損減唯事勝義執，名損減想。
彼於此想能正除遣，能斷、能捨，故名除遣。如是等類無量聖言，名為至教。由此如來最勝至教，應知諸法離言自性。
items.en: With respect to this percept, one is able to correctly eliminate it — able to cut it off, and able to abandon it — this is called "elimination." Immeasurable holy words of this kind and others are called scriptural authority. By means of the Tathāgata's own most excellent scriptural authority, it should be understood that phenomena possess an inexpressible nature.

items.title: Section: Resolving the Paradox — Why the Buddha Uses Language to Teach What Language Cannot Reach

items.zh: 問：若如是者，何因緣故，於一切法離言自性而起言說？
items.en: Question: If this is so, for what reason does one give rise to speech at all regarding phenomena's inexpressible nature?

items.zh: 答：若不起言說，則不能為他說一切法離言自性，他亦不能聞如是義。若無有聞，則不能知此一切法離言自性。為欲令他聞知諸法離言自性，是故於此離言自性而起言說。
items.en: Answer: If one did not give rise to speech, one would be unable to teach others that phenomena possess an inexpressible nature, nor would they be able to hear this meaning. Without hearing it, they would have no way to know that phenomena possess this inexpressible nature. It is precisely in order to let others hear and know that phenomena possess an inexpressible nature that speech is given rise to regarding this very inexpressible nature.

items.title: Section: How Unenlightened Discrimination Generates the Entire World of Experience

items.zh: 又諸愚夫，由於如是所顯真如不了知故，從是因緣，八分別轉，能生三事，能起一切有情世間及器世間。
items.en: Moreover, unenlightened beings, because they fail to understand the suchness just revealed, on account of this very cause, generate eight kinds of discrimination, which are able to produce three things — and these are able to give rise to the entire world of sentient beings and the entire physical world.

items.title: The Eight Kinds of Discrimination, Defined One by One

items.zh: 云何名為八種分別？一者、自性分別，二者、差別分別，三者、總執分別，四者、我分別，五者、我所分別，六者、愛分別，七者、非愛分別，八者、彼俱相違分別。
items.en: What are the eight kinds of discrimination? The first is discrimination of a thing's own nature; the second is discrimination of distinguishing features; the third is discrimination of a totalizing grasp; the fourth is discrimination of "I"; the fifth is discrimination of "mine"; the sixth is discrimination of what is liked; the seventh is discrimination of what is disliked; the eighth is discrimination of what is neither liked nor disliked.

items.zh: 云何如是八種分別能生三事？謂若自性分別、若差別分別、若總執分別，此三分別能生分別戲論所依、分別戲論所緣事。謂色等想事為依緣故，名想言說所攝、名想言說所顯分別戲論，即於此事分別計度非一眾多品類差別。

items.title: Section: How the Eight Discriminations Generate the Three Things — Samsara's Wheel Traced to Its Root

items.zh: 若我分別、若我所分別，此二分別能生一切餘見根本及慢根本薩迦耶見，及能生一切餘慢根本所有我慢。若愛分別、若非愛分別、若彼俱相違分別，如其所應能生貪欲、瞋恚、愚癡。
items.en: The discrimination of "I" and the discrimination of "mine" — these two discriminations are able to generate the view of a substantial self, which is the root of every other view and the root of pride; and they are able to generate self-pride, which is the root of every other kind of pride. The discrimination of what is liked, what is disliked, and what is neither — these, as is appropriate, are able to generate craving, hatred, and delusion.

items.zh: 是名八種分別，能生如是三事。謂分別戲論所依緣事，見、我慢事，貪瞋癡事。
當知此中，分別戲論所依緣事為所依止，生薩迦耶見及以我慢；薩迦耶見、我慢為依，生貪瞋癡。由此三事，普能顯現一切世間流轉品法。
items.en: It should be understood that, resting on the very basis and objects of discriminative conceptual proliferation, the view of a substantial self and pride arise; and resting on the view of a substantial self and pride, craving, hatred, and delusion arise. By means of these three things, the entire cycling of the world through its conditioned states becomes fully manifest.

items.zh: 云何名為自性分別？謂於一切色等想事，分別色等種種自性所有尋思。如是名為自性分別。云何名為差別分別？謂即於彼色等想事，謂此有色、謂此無色，謂此有見、謂此無見，謂此有對、謂此無對，謂此有漏、謂此無漏，謂此有為、謂此無為，謂此是善、謂此不善、謂此無記，謂此過去、謂此未來、謂此現在。由如是等無量品類差別道理，即於自性分別依處，分別種種彼差別義。如是名為差別分別。云何名為總執分別？謂即於彼色等想事，我及有情、命者、生者等假想施設所引分別。於總多法總執為因，分別而轉。於舍、軍、林、飲食、衣乘等假想施設所引分別，如是名為總執分別。云何名為我、我所分別？謂若諸事有漏有取，長時數習我、我所執之所積聚；由宿串習彼邪執故，自見處事為緣所生虛妄分別。如是名為我、我所分別。

items.title: Refining the Eight Discriminations — And Why Nothing Is Inherently Attractive or Repulsive

items.zh: 云何名為愛分別？謂緣淨妙、可意事境所生分別。云何名為非愛分別？謂緣不淨妙、不可意事境所生分別。云何名為彼俱相違分別？謂緣淨妙不淨妙、可意不可意俱離事境所生分別。
items.en: What is discrimination of what is liked? It is the discrimination arising with respect to an object taken to be pure, wondrous, and agreeable. What is discrimination of what is disliked? It is the discrimination arising with respect to an object taken to be impure, unwondrous, and disagreeable. What is discrimination of what is neither? It is the discrimination arising with respect to an object taken to be neither pure nor impure, neither agreeable nor disagreeable.

items.zh: 此中所說略有二種。一者、分別自性，二者、分別所依、分別所緣事。

blocks.text: A paradox resolved, then an account of how mistaken discrimination produces the whole world of experience. A passage (0489c29) is untranslated.
The "perception of earth" is the imputed designation "earth". To "eliminate" it is to "cut it off, abandon it": to let go of the imputation while the event remains.

subs.head: Why speak of what cannot be spoken?

blocks.text: "If one did not speak, one could not teach others that phenomena are inexpressible, nor could they hear it." Language is used to point beyond itself.

"Because unenlightened beings fail to understand suchness, they generate eight kinds of discrimination, which produce three things, and these give rise to the entire world of beings and the physical world."

Discrimination of a thing's **own nature**; of its **distinguishing features**; **totalising** ("self", "being", "house", "army", "forest"); of **I**; of **mine**; of **the liked**; of **the disliked**; and of **what is neither**.

The untranslated prose (0489c29) defines the first five: own nature is thinking "this is form", and so on; distinguishing features are "this is visible or invisible, contaminated or not, conditioned or unconditioned, good or bad, past or future"; totalising is naming collections as one; "I" and "mine" arise from long habituation to self-grasping.

The first three discriminations produce **the basis and object of proliferation**; "I" and "mine" produce **identity view and pride**; the last three produce **greed, hatred, and delusion**. As the treatise goes on to say, the liked and disliked are discriminations about objects "taken to be" pure or impure, agreeable or not.

quiz.q: "Able to eliminate this percept — to cut it off, to abandon it." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "cut off"?
options: preventing unarisen ones from arising, and stopping arisen ones from continuing
quiz.why: "With respect to this percept, one is able to correctly eliminate it — able to cut it off, and able to abandon it — this is called 'elimination.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: making unarisen ones not arise, and stopping arisen ones from continuing — that's "able to cut off."

quiz.q: "Why give rise to speech regarding the inexpressible nature?" How does Master Cháng Bǎi answer?
options: to let beings know the inexpressible nature, the Buddha speaks of it
quiz.why: "It is precisely in order to let others hear and know that phenomena possess an inexpressible nature that speech is given rise to regarding this very inexpressible nature." Master Cháng Bǎi: to let beings know the inexpressible nature of things, the Buddha gives rise to speech about it.

quiz.q: Eight discriminations "give rise to the world of beings and the physical world." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish them?
options: the beings' world is the five aggregates as primary result; the physical world the dependent environment — mountains, rivers, earth
quiz.why: "On account of this very cause, generate eight kinds of discrimination, which are able to produce three things — and these are able to give rise to the entire world of sentient beings and the entire physical world." Master Cháng Bǎi: the world of beings is the five aggregates as primary karmic result; the physical world is the dependent environment, including mountains, rivers, and the earth.

quiz.q: The I- and mine-discriminations "generate 薩迦耶見." How does Venerable Miào Jìng say this is rendered in Chinese?
quiz.why: "The discrimination of 'I' and the discrimination of 'mine' — these two discriminations are able to generate the view of a substantial self, which is the root of every other view and the root of pride." Venerable Miào Jìng: 薩迦耶 is rendered in Chinese as "view of the perishing aggregate."

quiz.q: "Discrimination of the liked arises towards objects taken as pure and agreeable." How do the masters view beauty and ugliness?
options: Cháng Bǎi: one finds someone beautiful, others may not; Miào Jìng: the mind's power makes objects appear so — none truly are
quiz.why: "What is discrimination of what is liked? It is the discrimination arising with respect to an object taken to be pure, wondrous, and agreeable." Master Cháng Bǎi: you find someone very beautiful, but others don't necessarily! Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind's dominant power makes objects appear in all kinds of similar forms — none actually are. That's a good explanation!
